'''''Dendrobium fleckeri''''', commonly known as the '''apricot cane orchid''',<ref name="Jones">{{cite book|last1=Jones|first1=David L.|title=A complete guide to native orchids of Australia including the island territories|date=2006|publisher=New Holland|location=Frenchs Forest, N.S.W.|isbn=1877069124|pages =404–405}}</ref> is a species of [[Epiphyte|epiphytic]] or [[Lithophyte|lithophytic]] orchid [[Endemism|endemic]] to [[far north Queensland]], Australia. It has cylindrical [[pseudobulb]]s with two or three dark green leaves and up to four [[wikt:apricot#Noun|apricot]]-coloured or yellowish green flowers with tangled white hairs on the edge of the [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]].

==Description==
''Dendrobium fleckeri'' is an epiphytic or lithophytic [[Herbaceous plant|herb]] that has cylindrical pseudobulbs {{convert|150-400|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3-4|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide. The pseudobulbs are yellowish green with two or three dark green, egg-shaped leaves {{convert|50-80|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|20-25|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide on the end. The flowering stem emerges from the end of the pseudobulb and is {{convert|10-25|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long with up to four [[Resupination|resupinate]], usually apricot-coloured, sometimes yellowish green flowers {{convert|25-30|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and wide. The [[wikt:dorsal|dorsal]] [[sepal]] is {{convert|14-17|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, {{convert|6-8|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide and the [[wikt:lateral|lateral]] sepals are a similar length but wider. The [[petal]]s are {{convert|13-15|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and about {{convert|3|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide. The [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]] is white with a purplish tinge, about {{convert|10|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and wide with three lobes. The side lobes are relatively large, upright and pointed and the middle lobe has three keels and dense hairs on its edges. Flowering occurs between August and January.<ref name="Jones" /><ref name="ATROK">{{cite web |author1=D.L.Jones |author2=T.Hopley |author3=S.M.Duffy |author1-link=David L. Jones (botanist) |year=2010 |access-date=31 May 2021 |url=http://www.canbr.gov.au/cpbr/cd-keys/RFKOrchids/key/rfkorchids/Media/Html/Thelychiton_fleckeri.htm |title=Factsheet - ''Thelychiton fleckeri'' |website=[[Australian Tropical Rainforest Orchids]] |publisher=Centre for Australian National Biodiversity Research (CANBR), [[Australian Government]]}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Dendrobium fleckeri'' was first formally described in 1937 by [[Herman Rupp]] and [[Cyril Tenison White]] and the description was published in ''The Queensland Naturalist''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Dendrobium fleckeri''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/504290|publisher=APNI|accessdate=23 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="Rupp">{{cite journal |last1=Rupp |first1=Herman |last2=White |first2=Cyril Tenison |title=Two new dendrobs for North Queensland |journal=The Queensland Naturalist |date=1937 |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=25–26 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/206421#page/27/mode/1up |accessdate=23 November 2018}}</ref> The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''fleckeri'') honours [[Hugo Flecker]], a physician, natural historian, and founding president of the [[North Queensland Naturalists' Club]].<ref name="adb">{{cite book |last1=Pearn |first1=John H. |title=Flecker, Hugo (1884–1957) |chapter=Hugo Flecker (1884–1957) |url=https://adb.anu.edu.au/biography/flecker-hugo-10199 |publisher=Australian Dictionary of Biography |access-date=23 November 2018}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The apricot cane orchid grows in trees, shrubs and boulders in mist forest between Mount Finnigan and Mount Fisher on [[Cape York Peninsula]].<ref name="Jones" /><ref name="ATROK" />
